To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
peripheral deafferentiation of the nodose or petrosal ganglions decreases the numbers of CGRP-ir and CGRP mRNA-containing visceral sensory neurons.
axotomy of visceral sensory neurons alters CGRP mRNA expression in the petrosol ganglion, and CGRP mRNA changes in the nodose ganglia are not detected with immunocytochemical techniques.
peripheral deafferentiation of visceral sensory neurons in the nodose and perrosal ganglia alters the expression of calcitonin-related peptide (CGR) mRNA in the perikarya of these ganglion cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of CGRP expression in visceral sensory perikaria of the petrosol and nodose ganglion and suggests that CGRP gene expression is altered in visceral afferent neurons after axotomy
the mechanisms of peripheral axotomy-induced changes of visceral sensory neurons.
the regulation of gene expression in visceral sensory ganglia and suggests that peripheral axotomy can alter gene expression in visceral afferent perikarya.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

axotomy-induced alterations of CGRP-ir and CGRP mRNA-containing visceral sensory perikaria of the nodose/petrosal ganglia may be due to changes in gene expression and may reflect the plasticity of the sensory nervous system.
peripheral deafferentiation of the nodose-petrosal ganglion complex alters the expression of CGRP mRNA in visceral sensory neurons.
axotomy-induced alterations in CGRP mRNA in the nodose and CGRP-ir cells in the petrosol ganglion are not correlated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CGRP mRNA expression in nodose and petroseal neurons is regulated by the peripheral input.
peripheral deafferentiation of visceral sensory neurons alters CGRP gene expression in the petrosol and nodose ganglion.
axotomy-induced alterations in the CGRP-ir population in the nodose and/or petrosal ganglions are dependent upon the specific afferent input which is removed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CGRP mRNA and CGRP immunoreactivity are not always correlated.
in situ hybridization can provide a powerful tool to evaluate changes in gene expression in peripheral neurons.
peripheral axotomy can alter the number of CGRP-ir and -mRNA-containing neurons in the visceral sensory ganglia.
